sourceClaimMap.claim: A private deed is not the same as changing registered title ranking.
Under the Land Title Act 1994 (Qld), registered instruments have priority according to when they were lodged, not according to when they were executed.

The priority of registered mortgages may be amended by registering an instrument amending priority, which must specify the order of all affected registered mortgages and be executed by all mortgagees affected.
On registration of that instrument, the mortgages have priority in the order specified.
Changing registered land-title order is a separate, formal process.
The Personal Property Securities Act 2009 includes default priority rules for security interests in personal property, and it also provides for voluntary subordination of security interests.
Those PPSA rules do not decide real-property mortgage ranking.

limitations: This is an automated independent editorial and source review, not human or professional financial approval.

That score was disregarded. This record replaces it. This review is https://cursor.com/agents/bc-94196b70-b134-5da2-9216-8a30c67fd16f.

Land Title Act 1994 (Qld) ss 77 and 178 were re-read from the in-force whole HTML (HTTP 200). Section 178(1) gives registered instruments priority by lodgement time, not execution time. Section 77 allows that mortgage priority to be amended only by registering an instrument that states the order of all affected registered mortgages and is executed by all mortgagees affected by the amendment; on registration, priority follows that order.

The declared PPSA URL is the Federal Register contents page for the 14 October 2024 compilation (HTTP 200) and lists s 55 Default priority rules and s 61 Voluntary subordination of security interests. The operative text was re-read from that same compilation: s 10 defines personal property as property other than land; s 8(1)(f)(i) excludes an interest provided for by the creation or transfer of an interest in land, except that ss 117 and 118 can apply to enforcement where the same obligation is also secured by personal property. Section 118(12) says those provisions do not modify land law. Default priority and voluntary subordination therefore do not decide registered real-property mortgage ranking.
